sentences.text: As all these Land Acquisition Appeals relate to the same acquisition proceedings for the construction of an approach road to the Cheekkal Kadavu Bridge in Karunagappally, they are taken up together for consideration and disposed by this common judgment.
2. The brief facts necessary for the disposal of these Land Acquisition Appeals are as follows:

The notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act for the acquisition of land for the purposes of construction of the approach road to the Cheekkal Kadavu Bridge in Karunagappally was published on 24.12.2009.
The possession of the acquired properties was taken on 12.11.2010 and the Land Acquisition Officer passed the award on 11.11.2010.

While determining the compensation payable to the land owners, the Land Acquisition Officer relied upon a Sale Deed No. 2353/2006 dated 01.11.2006 in relation to a property that was situated about 5.5 K.Ms away from the acquired property, and fixed the market value of the land at Rs.29,143/- per Are.
In relation to an extent of 0.96 Ares which was also acquired, the Land Acquisition Officer fixed the market value at Rs.12,143/- per Are.
3. Aggrieved by the market value fixed by the Land Acquisition Officer, the claimant landowners approached the court of Principal Sub Judge, Kollam.

LA.APP. NO. 83 OF 2017 6 2025:KER:39200 LA.APP. NO. 84 OF 2017 LA.APP. NO. 85 OF 2017  &
LA.APP. NO. 90 OF 2017

Before the said Reference Court, the appellants/claimants relied on Ext.A1 Sale Deed No.2001/2006 dated 23.06.2006 under which an extent of 12.5 cents of land had been sold at a price that was equivalent to Rs.74,130/- per Are.

The Reference Court, however, did not accept the market value shown in Ext.A1 sale deed despite the fact that the property covered by the said sale deed was situated in close proximity to the acquired land, solely because it was found from the 'notes on award' that a local enquiry by the officials had disclosed that the document was willfully executed at the preliminary stage of land acquisition proceedings with an intention to get a high value for the property.

The Reference Court, therefore, felt that the land value shown in Ext.A1 sale deed could not be straight away adopted, and chose instead to enhance the value arrived at by the Land Acquisition Officer by 65%.

The Reference Court accordingly fixed the market value of the land at Rs.48,086/- per Are and Rs.24,042/- per Are in respect of 0.96 Ares which had been treated differently even by the Land Acquisition Officer.

4. In the appeals before us, it is the submission of Sri.Siju Kamalasanan the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants that there was no justification whatsoever for the Reference Court to disbelieve the value shown in Ext.A1 Sale Deed that pertained to a property that was in close proximity to the acquired land and further, that the said market value pertained to the year 2006 Pappachan vs The State Of Kerala on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101551195/
5 and the Section 4(1) notification in the instant appeal was only on 24.12.2009.

It is also his submission that the suspicion of the Land Acquisition Officer regarding possible inflation of the market value of the land covered in Ext.A1 Sale Deed is also unfounded since it is highly improbable that the Land LA.APP. NO. 83 OF 2017 7 2025:KER:39200 LA.APP. NO. 84 OF 2017 LA.APP. NO.
85 OF 2017 & LA.APP. NO. 90 OF 2017 Acquisition Officer could have foreseen the initiation of an acquisition proceedings more than three years later.
5. We have also heard the learned Senior Government Pleader Sri.T.K.Shajahan on behalf of the respondent State.
Sri .T.K.Shajahan, the learned Senior Government Pleader would justify the judgment of the Reference Court and submits that the market value fixed by the Reference Court need not be interfered with.

6. On a consideration of the rival submissions, we find force in the submissions of Sri.Siju Kamalasanan, the learned counsel for the appellants/claimants that there could have been no legitimate basis for the stand of the Land Acquisition Officer that the market value shown in Ext.A1 Sale Deed was an inflated one taking note of a possible acquisition that would be initiated in the locality almost three years later.

No doubt, the fact that the Cheekkal Kadavu Bridge had already been constructed in the locality might have weighed with the vendors in Ext.A1 Sale Deed for the purposes of demanding a higher price for the land by showing the inevitability of an approach road being constructed sometime in the near future.
But that by itself would not be sufficient ground to disbelieve the value and adopt the same with minor adjustments to arrive at the market value of the properties covered by the present acquisition.

In our view, the mere fact that Ext.A1 Sale Deed was executed in the year 2006, and the acquisition proceedings in the instant case were initiated three years later, would suffice for us to adopt the market value shown in Ext.A1 sale deed, albeit without applying any LA.APP.

NO. 83 OF 2017 8 2025:KER:39200 LA.APP. NO. 84 OF 2017 LA.APP. NO.
85 OF 2017 & LA.APP. NO. 90 OF 2017 incremental factor for the three years that lapsed between the date of execution of Ext.A1 Sale Deed and the date of the Section 4(1) notification in the instant case.
We are, therefore, of the view that the market value of the property covered by the present acquisition can be safely fixed at Rs.74,130/- per Are as in Ext.A1 Sale Deed.

We might also add that in view of the judgment of the Supreme Court in Besco Case [Besco Ltd. vs The State Of Haryana [2023 SCC Online SC 1071]] , where the belting system was dispensed with, we do not see it necessary to accord a different treatment to the 0.96 Ares of land that was also acquired under the present acquisition proceedings.

sentences.text: Resultantly, the same market value of Rs.74,130/- per Are would also apply in respect of the 0.96 Ares that was dealt with differently by the Land Acquisition Officer at first instance and the Reference Court in the Reference proceedings.

Although the appellants /claimants also raised a plea with regard to the claim for injurious affection, we find that there was no evidence adduced before the Reference Court to support the said claim.
These Land Acquisition Appeals, are therefore, allowed by refixing the market value of the acquired lands as Rs.74,130/- per Are.
The appellants/claimants shall be entitled to a revised computation of the compensation due to them under the Act on the above basis.
They shall also be entitled to all statutory benefits including proportionate cost, that flow from the above revised fixation of the market value.
The appellants/claimants shall not be entitled to the statutory interest for the period covering the delay occasioned while filing the appeals before this Court.
